nodes.label: Bluespec random-trial testbench pattern (rule r1 generates, rule r2 compares vs * operator)
nodes.author: M.K.Sanju Vikasini, K.Sreenidhi
nodes.norm_label: bluespec random-trial testbench pattern (rule r1 generates, rule r2 compares vs * operator)
nodes.rationale: Each design is checked over m trials by comparing its result against the system's '*' operator; num and num2=2*num constants must be edited in the main BSV file and process_func.bsv.

nodes.label: Booth multiplication (iterative and pipelined 32/64-bit)
nodes.author: M.K.Sanju Vikasini, K.Sreenidhi
nodes.rationale: Signed (2's complement) multiplication; pipelined variants group iterations into stages (32-bit: 2x16, 4x8; 64-bit: 4x16, 8x8). Not integrated with the golden model, which handles unsigned products.

nodes.label: Radix-2 multiplication (radix_2.bsv)
nodes.author: M.K.Sanju Vikasini, K.Sreenidhi
nodes.rationale: Groups 2 multiplier bits to select 0, +1 or -1 times multiplicand; cycles reduced to n/8 by doing 8 steps per cycle.

nodes.label: Radix-4 multiplication (radix_4.bsv)
nodes.author: M.K.Sanju Vikasini, K.Sreenidhi
nodes.rationale: Groups 3 multiplier bits to select 0, +-1, +-2 times multiplicand giving n/2 terms; cycles reduced to n/8 by doing 4 steps per cycle.

nodes.label: Shift and Add multiplication (plus and adder variants, 1-4 steps/cycle)
nodes.author: M.K.Sanju Vikasini, K.Sreenidhi
nodes.norm_label: shift and add multiplication (plus and adder variants, 1-4 steps/cycle)
nodes.rationale: Plus variants use the built-in + operator; adder variants use an explicit full adder. one/two/three/four names give the number of algorithm iterations done in one cycle.

nodes.label: Pipelined Wallace multiplier (32-bit, variation of multi-cycle)
nodes.author: M.K.Sanju Vikasini, K.Sreenidhi
nodes.norm_label: pipelined wallace multiplier (32-bit, variation of multi-cycle)

nodes.label: Wallace tree multiplication (single-cycle, multi-cycle, pipelined)
nodes.author: M.K.Sanju Vikasini, K.Sreenidhi
nodes.rationale: Partial products are grouped in threes and reduced to sum and carry rows until two rows remain, then ripple-added. Pipelined 32-bit version: 3 + (4*7) + 1 = 32 steps.

nodes.label: 100% coverage does not imply correctness
nodes.rationale: Coverage measures code that was written, so missing logic is invisible, errors can be masked, and REVERSI proves self-consistency rather than spec conformance.

nodes.label: REVERSI Rule 1: test instruction only in modification
nodes.norm_label: reversi rule 1: test instruction only in modification
nodes.rationale: Using the instruction under test to also restore lets a systematic fault cancel itself out, so broken hardware would pass.

nodes.label: REVERSI Rule 2: handle information loss
nodes.rationale: Lossy instructions such as shift-left need control code to preserve bits; fully non-invertible ops (ABS, floating point rounding) defeat REVERSI.

nodes.label: Golden-model tension between PATARA and Vector Accelerator papers
nodes.norm_label: golden-model tension between patara and vector accelerator papers
nodes.rationale: PATARA reaches 100% code coverage without a reference model; the Vector Accelerator paper uses Spike and found 3,005 errors and taped out. High coverage and high bug yield are not the same thing.

nodes.label: Three comparison tensions (golden model, systematic vs random vs proof, scalability vs completeness)
nodes.norm_label: three comparison tensions (golden model, systematic vs random vs proof, scalability vs completeness)
nodes.rationale: Each tension has papers on both sides, which turns the comparison from a summary into an argument.
